title: NetlistBench: Evaluating LLM Reliability in SPICE Netlist Recognition and Manipulation
abstract: arXiv:2608.12197v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly used in circuit design workflows, yet their reliability on simulator-facing SPICE netlist recognition and manipulation remains poorly understood and is rarely separated from high-level design reasoning. Although netlists are textual, they encode structured circuit objects through topology and parameters. We present \textbf{NetlistBench}, a structure-verified benchmark for SPICE netlist recognition and manipulation. NetlistBench contains 2,342 cases across 24 task families, covering parameter and connectivity recognition and edits, hierarchical operations, equivalence judgment, and long-horizon compound editing. Model outputs are evaluated by a deterministic structure-aware oracle. Across six non-thinking LLMs, performance varies substantially with operation-level structural complexity. Simple local edits reach $96\%$--$100\%$ accuracy, while device addition drops to $41\%$--$83\%$ and equiv

translated_title: NetlistBench：评估大型语言模型在SPICE网表识别与操作中的可靠性
translated_abstract: 大型语言模型（LLMs）越来越多地用于电路设计流程中，但它们在与模拟器交互的SPICE网表识别和操作方面的可靠性仍未被充分理解，并且很少与高层设计推理分开研究。尽管网表是文本形式的，但通过拓扑和参数编码了结构化的电路对象。我们提出了NetlistBench，一个用于SPICE网表识别和操作的结构验证基准。NetlistBench包含24个任务族中的2342个案例，涵盖参数和连接识别与编辑、层次操作、等价性判断以及长时程复合编辑。模型输出由确定性的结构感知oracle评估。在六个非思考型LLM中，性能随操作级结构复杂性显著变化。简单的局部编辑准确率达到96%至100%，而器件添加降至41%至83%，等价性判断的准确率则更低。
tldr: 本论文提出了NetlistBench，一个结构验证的基准测试，用于评估大型语言模型在SPICE网表识别和操作中的可靠性，发现性能随操作复杂性显著变化，简单编辑准确率高而复杂操作准确率低。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces NetlistBench, a structure-verified benchmark to evaluate LLM reliability in SPICE netlist recognition and manipulation, revealing performance varies substantially with operation complexity, with high accuracy on simple edits but low on complex operations.
